title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): for a finite flat group scheme G (truncated Barsotti-Tate or more general, killed by p in this computation) over an arbitrary base S, Grothendieck wants a Dieudonné crystal D*(G) on S_cris with F: D^(p) -> D and V: D -> D^(p), FV = p, VF = 0. He wants to describe it through the co-Lie complexes ℓ_G and ℓ_{G*}, which are perfect of amplitude [-1,0], and a pairing between them. The goal is distinguished triangles of the form φ*(ℓ_{G*})^∨[-1] -> φ*(ℓ_G) -> D*_cris(G) -> (triangle I on S_cris; triangles II and III in other incarnations). These are complex-level versions of the Hodge filtration 0 -> ω_G -> D(G) -> Lie(G*) -> 0. The previous page even suggests a two-term complex D*_cris(G) with H^0 = D*(G) and H^1 = D_*(G).

This page checks that the triangle respects (F,V)-structures. It sets ℓ, ℓ' to be the two co-Lie-type complexes with V_ℓ: ℓ -> ℓ^(p) and F_ℓ = 0, and similarly for ℓ'; Frobenius is zero on the Lie/co-Lie pieces. Δ* is the middle term of triangle III, with:
- i_0: ℓ[-1] -> Δ*;
- π_0: Δ* -> ℓ'^∨;
- the connecting map ∂_0: ℓ'^∨ -> ℓ[-1].
F_{Δ*} and V_{Δ*} are written as composites of the triangle maps: F_{Δ*} = ε*(i_II) ∘ π_0^(p) and V_{Δ*} = i_0^(p) ∘ ε*(π_II), using a second triangle II pulled back by ε*.

Claim 1: III is an (F,V)-triangle. The checks are:
- i_0 compatible with V: V_{Δ*} ∘ i_0 = i_0^(p) ∘ ε*(π_II) ∘ i_0 = i_0^(p) ∘ V_{ℓ[-1]}, using ε*(π_II) ∘ i_0 = V_{ℓ[-1]}.
- π_0 compatible with F, and dually with V.
- ∂_0 compatible with F: ∂_0 ∘ π_0 ∘ ε*(i_II) = 0, matching F = 0 on ℓ[-1]. The same holds for V.

Claim 2: the identification φ*(III) ≅ I, where I is the triangle built from the Dieudonné module M with F: M^(p) -> M and V: M -> M^(p), respects F and V. This reduces to φ*(V_ℓ[-1]) = V_{[M^(p) -F-> M]} and φ*(F_{ℓ'}[-1]) = F_{[M -V-> M^(p)]}. The first is proved by functoriality: φ*(ε*(π_II) i_0) = π_II^(p) i_I = V. The second 'se prouve de même'.

This is routine homological bookkeeping inside the program of describing the Dieudonné crystal by co-Lie complexes (Grothendieck's Montréal 1970 programme).
errors: Indices and twists are inconsistently written: the target of the first identity reads V_{[M^(p) -F-> M]}, while the final line writes V_{[M^(p) -> M]}. The term '[M^∨ -F-> M]' in the machine transcription is almost surely M^(p).
The line 'on voit de même que π_0 compatible avec F' duplicates an earlier conclusion. The symmetric verifications (π_0 with V, ∂_0 with V, the second identity in 2) are only asserted, not checked.
Signs and the precise definition of F_{Δ*}, V_{Δ*} as composites are left implicit, so the compatibilities hold only modulo those conventions.

ideas.what: Dieudonné crystal of a finite flat / truncated BT group over an arbitrary base, with F, V structure
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal, 1974); ICM 1970 talk

ideas.what: Hodge filtration of the Dieudonné crystal expressed as a distinguished triangle involving co-Lie complexes ℓ_G, ℓ_{G*}
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration of D(G) / co-Lie complex description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Illusie (Complexe cotangent; Déformations de groupes de BT, 1985), BBM
ideas.where_published: partly in the Montréal notes; co-Lie complex in Illusie

ideas.what: Verification that the triangle maps i_0, π_0, ∂_0 commute with F and V (F = 0, V on Lie complexes)

missed.claim: This page belongs to an attempt (previous page) to define, for arbitrary finite flat G over arbitrary bases, a two-term crystalline Dieudonné complex D*_cris(G) with H^0 = D*(G) and H^1 = D_*(G), compatible with F, V via co-Lie triangles. The present page only checks F-V compatibility of the triangles, and the general programme was not completed in this form.
missed.quote: le triangle (III) est compatible avec (F,V)-structures ... L'isom. φ*(III) ≃ I compatible avec (F-V)-structures
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild precursor of derived/complex-valued Dieudonné theories for finite flat group schemes (BBM Ext-sheaves, later prismatic Dieudonné theory). The page itself is routine verification, though.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine diagram check of F/V compatibility for triangles in Grothendieck's known programme of Dieudonné crystals via co-Lie complexes. Any interest lies in the surrounding pages' idea of a two-term Dieudonné complex, not in this page.
